title: One rule set, one pinned dictionary version, its read path and the allow-list approver after the marks became reference data
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 20, 29, 35, 47; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.4 and R5.5 (DP-01, DP-05, DP-07, DP-08, DP-19); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rows sys_fields, party_ext, interaction, document_field; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 011 PDPA lint for code tests and logs v1.md
section: Section 3 Preconditions; Section 7 AC11; Section 11 Data; Section 12.2; Section 13 Solution plan
description: The sources fix the principles but not the mechanics. No source says how a rule set generated once in the service template is shared by all 19 generated repositories at one version, which operation of the reference-data contract serves the dictionary and its version, how a version is pinned and recorded per build, how a per-service sys_fields seed in a repository relates to rwb-source-data's sys_fields registry now that the marks are reference data, which role approves an allow-list change once the approval is an authorisation decision, or where the release quality view of findings per repository, per gate and per dictionary version is published. This story applies working defaults for all six and records them as three assumptions.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 11 fixes contract-first and contract tests in every build but names no dictionary contract; slide 20 gives every service the template but names no shared rule-set version; slide 29 forbids a cross-schema read but names no read path for the marks; slide 35 places personal data in the owning service but names no approver role for a build-configuration change; slide 47 names the boundary test and the grant review but no release quality view. Template and Rules R5.5 gives DP-07 and DP-08 as the contract patterns and no path. The Ownership Map puts sys_fields with P1 rwb-source-data and gives no dictionary operation. The legacy story reads a sys_fields seed file and a code-owner approval, neither of which survives the split unchanged.
proposed: Confirm with the solution architect and the platform team: the dictionary is served by the reference-data contract of rwb-case from rwb_source_data's sys_fields without a second registry, the rule set is generated once from a pinned version and inherited by the 19 repositories through the template, the build record carries the dictionary and rule-set versions, the approver of an allow-list change is the repository's code-owner role resolved through the authorise contract, and the release quality view is a gateway-bff composite route published by RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: Owner, instance, run-record surface and reporting of the daily decision log hash-chain check after the split
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-14, 02:00, owner rwb-decision, mechanism Schedule), slide 14 (rwb-decision Schedules: rule promote 00:01, chain check 02:00), slide 28 (recorded locally, collected centrally, chain checked every day, sealed daily), slide 20 (every service writes its own decision record and publishes DecisionRecorded), slide 29 (one schema and one login per service); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12 and 16 (workflow kit layer L3; JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json jobs JOB-13 and JOB-14; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 008 Decision log hash chain check v1.md sections 12 and 13
description: The sources say the chain check runs at 02:00 as a Temporal Schedule owned by rwb-decision and that each of the 19 services writes and chains its own decision records, but no source fixes the schedule ID and display name, the catch-up and backfill semantics, which instance owns which chain after the split, how the retired decision-log copy job's wait is replaced, where the run records are read from and how long they are kept, or through which channel Compliance is told (the ACE notification path or a service) and whether the ingest completeness of a business date is published at all.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-14 with owner rwb-decision, time 02:00 and mechanism Schedule and nothing more; slide 14 names Schedules: chain check 02:00 only; the Temporal design slide 16 says JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00 without a schedule name; the legacy contract table names a Quartz cron, an ACE job run record and the ACE notification path, and none of those objects survives the move to Temporal Schedules and to the per-service schemas.
area: Temporal schedules, decision log, compliance reporting
proposed: Fix the schedule ID, the catch-up and backfill rule and the run-record retention in the schedule catalog published with RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; have rwb-decision publish the ingest completeness state of a business date; keep the ACE notification path for the three reports and record that choice in the run book of the legacy JOB-14.

title: One storage set or one per service, the container naming standard, the home of the retention period and the retention classes, the name of the retention Schedule and the readiness surface are not fixed once only rwb-document may reach the containers
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 012 Document storage containers v1.md sections 3, 4 and 13; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 7, 9, 16, 20, 29, 41 and 44; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 12 and 32; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5, R7 and R9; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables document, document_field and document_type; API rows POST /cases/{caseId}/documents, GET /documents/{documentId}, POST /documents and GET /documents/{documentId}/content; job JOB-17)
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 12.6 Schedules; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: RWB-TE-012 sets up one storage account per environment with a private endpoint and the four containers rwb-intake, rwb-docs, rwb-docs-legal and rwb-quarantine for the whole monolith, and fixes the account settings, the policies and the role assignments from the ACE storage pattern. Arch v5 gives the store to rwb-document alone (slides 9, 16, 29 and 41) and gives the retention run to the same service as a Temporal Schedule (slide 44, JOB-17, monthly on the 1st Sunday), so five values have no source after the split: whether one storage account and one set of four containers per environment stay shared by the 19 services or become one set per service when only rwb-document may reach them; the naming standard of a container in the target, since the legacy names come from the ACE standard and no target source restates it; where the retention period and the retention classes are held now that they are a parameter and a reference row, and which row decides the container and the period of a document type; the name of the retention Schedule and whether its cadence is a parameter, a reference row or the literal job-map value; and the exact surface on which the readiness is read, since the legacy story names the interface and job monitor screen while the target reads a service health endpoint behind gateway-bff.
evidence: RWB-TE-012 section 3: 'The ACE storage pattern is used (DL27, option A recommended): one storage account per environment in the SCB tenant with a private endpoint'; section 4 step 2: 'creates the containers rwb-intake, rwb-docs, rwb-docs-legal and rwb-quarantine'; section 13: 'Template parameters: legalRetentionDays 3650 (assumed; DL26), legalPolicyLocked true in PROD only, softDeleteDays 30 (assumed; DL27)'. Architecture v5 slide 29: 'Blob storage with WORM: documents (rwb-document only)'; slide 16: 'TMP DocumentIntakeWorkflow: OCR, classify, extract - Act: generate, seal - Schedule: retention' and 'FILE Azure Blob (WORM): files, 2.8 TB by 2031'; slide 44 JOB-17 'Retention | monthly, 1st Sunday | rwb-document | Schedule', with the note 'a Temporal Schedule (cron, with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window)'; slide 20: 'REST /health, /metrics for the platform' and 'Own task queue rwb-<svc>; its own Schedules'. ownership.json JOB-17: owner P5, replacement 'Temporal Schedule retention in rwb-document'. No source read states an account count per service, a target container naming standard, the row that holds the retention period or the classes, the name of the Schedule, or the readiness surface.
proposed: Fix the five values at the wave 0 storage review with the platform lead, the rwb-document tech lead, the security architect and Compliance for the retention class: the account and container count per environment, the container naming standard, the parameter and the reference row that hold each retention value and class, the name of the retention Schedule with its cadence, and the readiness surface. Each value is a parameter or a reference row, so closing one needs no code change; the defaults recorded in ASM-B-PLT-TPL-03-TE012-1, ASM-B-PLT-TPL-03-TE012-2 and ASM-B-PLT-TPL-03-TE012-3 apply until then.
